$comment: Single source of truth for Field Guide box-category styling (colorClass + badge icon/name). Read by dm.html at runtime (fetched into SCC_FG_CATEGORY_STYLE) and by scripts/fg-template.mjs (check/build). Edit this file, not a hardcoded copy in either place — see CLAUDE.md Decision Log for the original SCC_FG_CATEGORY_STYLE object this was extracted from.

$specialCasedCategories.$comment: These box categories are NOT in `categories` above -- they never read colorClass/badge from this table at all, because sccFgRenderBlock() dispatches them to their own dedicated render function before the generic box case (which is the only consumer of `categories`) ever runs. Listed here so fg-template.mjs's `check` command knows they're recognized categories without treating their absence from `categories` as an unknown-category error. Do not add entries for these to `categories` -- that would imply they use the generic colorClass/badge box rendering, which they don't.
$specialCasedCategories.spoken_dialogue_note: spoken_dialogue IS also a real key in `categories` above (its own dedicated render function, sccFgRenderSpokenDialogue, reads categories.spoken_dialogue directly for its badge) -- it is not special-cased out of the table, just special-cased out of the *generic* box render path. Listed here only for cross-reference, not as an extra recognized-but-untabled category.
$specialCasedCategories.comedy_inline_note: comedy (with block.inline === true) is likewise a real key in `categories` -- sccFgRenderComedyInline() also reads categories.comedy for consistency, it just renders as a plain inline paragraph instead of a colored box shell. Not a separate category name.
$specialCasedCategories.quest_beats: Live, clickable quest-beat status widget (sccFgRenderQuestBeatsBlock). Ignores block.color/category styling entirely -- pulls its own content from SCC_SELECTED.quest + the quests table, not from any box color scheme.
$specialCasedCategories.combat_outcomes: Branching combat-outcome log widget (sccFgRenderCombatOutcomesBlock). Header now renders the real player_decision chip (see `categories` above) instead of a hardcoded icon+label, but the box shell itself still has its own fixed styling, no colorClass/badge lookup for the shell.
$specialCasedCategories.scenario_cards: Scenario Cards navigation module (sccFgRenderScenarioCardsBlock, 2026-08-26 rebuild) -- any-length array of cards, each with an optional entity portrait, rich block-array content (rendered via the same sccFgRenderDoc every other Field Guide content uses), and an optional decision selector (player_decision chip, click-to-log/unlog via the same shared session_note_entries mechanism combat_outcomes uses). Replaces the earlier scenario_tabs/approach_tracker categories entirely -- both are gone, not kept alongside this.
$specialCasedCategories.guide_meta_note: guide_meta IS a real key in `categories` above (colorClass grey, badge null) but sccFgRenderBlock() returns '' for it unconditionally before the generic box case is ever reached -- confirmed intentionally unrendered (the old 'How to Use This Guide' box), not a bug. Data is kept, never displayed.

$recognizedLinkTypes.$comment: The type vocabulary an inline [[type:id|Label]] link actually resolves to when clicked. Fixed 2026-08-27 (QA round 4, item 8): sccOpenLookup() (dm.html) now resolves its `type` argument through the same SCC_FG_FEATURED_TYPE_ALIASES map block.featured entries already used (npc->character, poi/nation->city) before dispatching to its type-specific branches, so [[poi:...]]/[[npc:...]]/[[nation:...]] links resolve correctly now -- previously sccOpenLookup had no dedicated branch for those raw type strings, so a well-formed [[poi:...]] link opened the lookup drawer to a permanent 'No details available.' with no real error. `types` here lists every type an inline link's click target actually resolves to, aliases included -- kept as its own list rather than reused verbatim from SCC_FG_LINK_TYPES's keys, since an author should still be free to write [[city:...]] directly for a real city and either [[poi:...]] or [[city:...]] for a POI -- both are valid authoring choices now.
